subject.title: feat(state): snapshot state DB before a forward schema migration

question: Should shared-state migrations be allowed to continue when the newly proposed automatic rollback snapshot fails, or must a failed snapshot block the forward version bump?
rationale: The branch deliberately selects best-effort backup creation, but that leaves the requested rollback guarantee unavailable under disk or permission failures; the correct availability-versus-recoverability contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Require a successful snapshot
options.body: Abort forward migration when a recoverable pre-migration copy cannot be created, prioritizing rollback safety over startup availability.

options.title: Keep best-effort snapshots
options.body: Allow migration to proceed with a clear warning when backup creation fails, preserving current startup availability while documenting the recovery limitation.

recommendation.title: Keep best-effort snapshots
recommendation.body: Allow migration to proceed with a clear warning when backup creation fails, preserving current startup availability while documenting the recovery limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied related PR context shows recent ownership of the same schema migration safety boundary.
